Jordan —

Attached are the technical artifacts you requested: dataflow_v1.svg (illustrates PII path for inference requests), access_matrix.csv (role -> data class access), and kms_attestation.txt (high-level KMS custody statement). See answers inline to your questions: 

- Production vs. test: By default PII enters the production inference fleet only. Test/dev environments are isolated; synthetic PII is permitted in test with explicit tagging and is not routed to production caches.

- Audit logs: We capture auth events (login, token issuance), admin actions (role grants, IAM changes), and data-access traces (per-request token metadata + model and route). Default retention: 12 months in the us-east-1 region. We can provide an export sample (CSV) under an NDA; sample available at: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-dataflow-diagrams (drive contains an anonymized audit export).

- KMS custody & backups: For hosted customers we use a regional CMK managed by Redwood; backups (encrypted snapshots) remain in the same region unless customer opts into cross-region replication for DR. For Redwood Private customers we support customer-managed keys (bring-your-own-KMS) with no plaintext key material leaving the customer's control. kms_attestation.txt explains cryptographic algorithms, envelope encryption approach, and backup handling.

Brief inline data flow (ASCII sketch):

Client -> API gateway (TLS) -> Request router -> Inference workers (KV cache) -> Model runtime -> Response
                   |                                        |
                   +-> Prefix cache (regionally cached, TTL)  +-> Audit logging (per-request metadata stored in logs)

Notes: KV cache stores ephemeral context only; no persistent PII storage is performed by default. Where customers choose persistent logs for debugging, we mark data classes and retain per agreed retention windows.

Next steps: if the artifacts look good to Acme we can: (a) populate the proposed_dpa_clause.docx with exact retention numbers, (b) produce the subprocessor CSV, and (c) run a short 30-minute walkthrough next week on the diagram. Let me know preferred times.

Thanks,
